corrections.from: Taking an inert pill, how much of it is taken, and a five-year mortality
corrections.finding: Three faults, and the item is otherwise sound and no duplicate. (1) A figure attached to the wrong group by its placement. "among 2,092 selves taking an inert pill in a second, 141 of them, 6.7%, take less than 75%, mortality comes at 14.8%" puts a bare "mortality" with the 141 as its nearest antecedent, where the source holds 14.8% as the whole inert-pill arm's mortality in that trial and not the less-adherent subgroup's; the subgroup's own rate is a different figure, and the item's own next clause gives that group's hazard ratio, so the reading the placement invites is the one the hazard ratio is the measure of. The fix names the denominator the item has already stated, "mortality across those 2,092 comes at 14.8%", adding no number. (2) A released word. "leaves the first trial's association alike at each outcome" stands "association" as the item's own noun for a measured relation. Natural Naming 2.6 releases it — "*Association* and *resonance* return that way to their coupling" — and the living file dissolves its twin at 4.4: "a correlation stands between two measurements, a coupling stands with a between, and only one of them is somewhere." Neither the living file nor the gathering-value file holds the bare word anywhere; the gathering-value file's four *associated* are each inside a field's own compound name, a field's word at a field's own result. What the source's adjustment acts on is its hazard-ratio estimates per outcome, and the item already says "the hazard ratio is" and "the hazard ratios are", so "hazard ratios" says it with the item's own word and adds nothing. *Attenuates* stays: it is the field's own word for its own result. (3) A part of the source dropped, where the dropping lets two pairs read as two populations. The 15.0/24.6 and 15.1/28.3 pairs are one trial's two arms, randomized, read at one same 80% threshold. The item gives no signal of that, and against its next sentence's "in one heart trial" and "in a second" a reader may count three or four separate studies — which is the force of the observing lost, since what the source holds is that the inert-pill arm's spread stands beside its own drug arm's within one trial. "two arms of one trial" is what the source holds and no more, and the comma before "with a lipid-lowering drug" goes so the phrase attaches to the pair it belongs to rather than floating over both. Named as supported: the 80% threshold does attach to both pairs already, carried by the shared subject "Selves taking 80% or more of their prescribed pills" through the coordinating "and", so nothing was needed there. Also fixed, same sentence: "the strongest stand at 55%" takes its noun, and the two cutoffs take "with the first" and "with the second", since both point estimates are 0.42 and position across four sentences was the only thing holding them apart — the place a figure gets crossed later. NOT corrected, with the reason: the first trial's own arm mortality stands absent where the second's is given, and I do not put it in. The published report holds it, but the item's source is a slice item I cannot read past its first eighty characters, so adding a number from the paper would be adding a number of my own to an item whose source may not have held it — the exact move an earlier reading's fix made. Flagged, left out. Sound otherwise. Every measure stands as the kind of measure it is: percentages of mortality said as percentages, hazard ratios named as hazard ratios and nowhere read as a risk or a percentage, and percentage thresholds of pills taken kept apart from both. No interval is inverted — each runs low to high with its point estimate inside it (0.52 in 0.38 to 0.71; 0.52 in 0.35 to 0.79; 0.89 in 0.84 to 0.95; 0.90 in 0.83 to 0.98; 0.75 in 0.49 to 1.15; 0.61 in 0.38 to 0.96; 0.77 in 0.49 to 1.22; 0.54 in 0.34 to 0.88; 0.42 in 0.27 to 0.66; 0.42 in 0.23 to 0.74), and no bound has lost its percent sign, the one "95% confidence interval" naming standing for the bare bounds after it as the gathering-value file's own idiom does at 1.4 and at its Droplets. The two trials' figures are not crossed: 1,255 with 98, 7.8% and 0.38 to 0.71 stand together and 2,092 with 141, 6.7%, 14.8% and 0.35 to 0.79 stand together, each as the source holds them, and the per-10%, lagged, cutoff and adjustment pairs each keep that same first-then-second order throughout. The two thresholds stay unmixed, 80% with the lipid-lowering pair and 75% with the two inert-pill trials, and the 50% to 95% range belongs to the cutoff variation alone. No association is stated as an observing of a cause: "hold a five-year mortality of", "stands with the higher taking", "the hazard ratios are", "comes at" and "stand at" carry every relation, and taking more of an inert pill is nowhere said to do anything. The quoted sentence stands at 4.2 word for word, once, and 4.2 is its place: non-adherence is listed there among the residue tells and the sentence is the file's own observing of non-compliance as the sharpest of them. No living file and no Droplet holds this value — 4.3's placebo-arm material is about adverse events returned and about leaving, not about how much of a pill is taken, and the Droplets' nearest, the statin n-of-1 months, holds symptom scores and months stopped early. No dissolving name stands in the text, no source, name, publishing, session, date, narrator or history, no hedge and no gate, and the degree words each carry their number or the field's own measuring.

fixed.section: 4.2 Clean cuts — where medicine reports no problem
fixed.sentence: It is a name a protocol gives to **a person's own parity across and both ways**, coming with their own between with their own rate, filed as a failure of a plan.
fixed.text: Selves taking 80% or more of their prescribed pills hold a five-year mortality of 15.0% against 24.6% among selves taking less with a lipid-lowering drug, and 15.1% against 28.3% with an inert pill, two arms of one trial. Among 1,255 selves taking an inert pill in one heart trial, 98 of them, 7.8%, take less than 75% of it, and an all-cause mortality hazard ratio of 0.52 stands with the higher taking, 95% confidence interval 0.38 to 0.71; among 2,092 selves taking an inert pill in a second, 141 of them, 6.7%, take less than 75%, mortality across those 2,092 comes at 14.8%, and the hazard ratio is 0.52, 0.35 to 0.79. Per 10% more of it taken the hazard ratios are 0.89, 0.84 to 0.95, and 0.90, 0.83 to 0.98. With the last adherence measuring dropped the hazard ratios are 0.75, 0.49 to 1.15, and 0.61, 0.38 to 0.96; with the last two dropped, 0.77, 0.49 to 1.22, and 0.54, 0.34 to 0.88. Varying the cutoff from 50% to 95%, the strongest hazard ratios stand at 55% with the first, 0.42, 0.27 to 0.66, and at 60% with the second, 0.42, 0.23 to 0.74. Adjusting for demographics, cardiovascular risk factors and education leaves the first trial's hazard ratios alike at each outcome and attenuates the second's at non-cardiovascular mortality.
